Calling SCWorkflow from the CLI

cli.Rmd

SCWorkflow includes an executable file called scworkflow. Any user-facing function in the SCWorkflow R package can be called with scworkflow [function] from the unix CLI. Function arguments are passed in via a JSON file. In addition to arguments used by the function, the JSON file can contain the following keys:

  • object_input_rds - file path to an existing object (Seurat object or SCWorkflow list) in RDS format. This is required if the SCWorkflow function has object as an argument (most user-facing functions do).
  • object_output_rds - file path to write the result to.

Run scworkflow --help to see the full CLI usage:

#> Registered S3 method overwritten by ‘quantmod’: #> method from #> as.zoo.data.frame zoo



Usage: SCWorkflow [function] [--json=path/to/args.json]

[function] should be the name of a function exported from SCWorkflow.
[--json] should specify the path to a JSON file with arguments accepted by that function. The equals sign (=) is required to separate --json from the path.

Additionally, the JSON file can contain the following keys:
  - object_input_rds: file path to an existing MultiOmicsDataset object in RDS format. This is required if `method` has `object` as an argument.
  - object_output_rds: file path to write the result to.

Use `scworkflow [function] --help` for more information about the associated function.

Main functions:
  scworkflow processRawData
  scworkflow filterQC
  scworkflow combineNormalize
  scworkflow annotateCellTypes
  scworkflow appendMetadataToSeuratObject
  scworkflow filterSeuratObjectByMetadata
  scworkflow reclusterFilteredSeuratObject
  scworkflow reclusterSeuratObject
  scworkflow degGeneExpressionMarkers
  scworkflow modScore
  scworkflow nameClusters
  scworkflow colorByGene
  scworkflow colorByMarkerTable
  scworkflow plotMetadata
  scworkflow dotPlotMet
  scworkflow violinPlot_mod
  scworkflow heatmapSC
  scworkflow tSNE3D
  scworkflow dualLabeling
  scworkflow harmonyBatchCorrect

Installing the SCWorkflow CLI

Installation on a personal computer

After installing the R package, you can use system.file() to locate the scworkflow executable file with R:

# remotes::install_github("CCBR/MOSuite", dependencies = TRUE)
system.file("exec", "scworkflow", package = "SCWorkflow")
#> [1] "/private/var/folders/wv/_vn77wl50f1_pyfx150ll75nldbfmw/T/Rtmp2lMLiR/temp_libpathbd5b1cd2df51/SCWorkflow/exec/scworkflow"

You should add this executable to your PATH environment variable.

export PATH="$PATH:/path/to/exec/scworkflow"

Example end-to-end script

You can create a shell script to run the full SCWorkflow pipeline. This script assumes you have a directory json_args/ with JSON files to set each function’s arguments.

The example script and accompanying JSON files are included in the package data. You can copy them to your working directory with R:

# copy the example script
file.copy(system.file("extdata", "TestRunjson.sh", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./")
# copy the JSON files
file.copy(system.file("extdata", "json_args", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./", recursive = TRUE)
# copy the test data files
file.copy(system.file("extdata", "chariou", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./", recursive = TRUE)

singularity shell --bind $(pwd):/mnt docker://nciccbr/scworkflow:v1.0.2-galaxy-5
cd /mnt
R -e 'file.copy(system.file("extdata", "TestRunjson.sh", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./")'
R -e 'file.copy(system.file("extdata", "json_args", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./", recursive = TRUE)'
R -e 'file.copy(system.file("extdata", "chariou", package = "SCWorkflow"), to = "./", recursive = TRUE)'

Then run the script from the CLI:

bash ./TestRunjson.sh

The .rds output for each function can be set in the corresponding .json file
